applicabilityBasis.summary: PYUSD is a Paxos-issued U.S. dollar payment stablecoin distributed by PayPal with 1:1 redemption and monthly reserve attestations.

genius.notes: Paxos Trust Company, N.A. is the PYUSD issuer, not PayPal or Paxos Issuance Europe Oy. The December 12, 2025 OCC decision conditionally approved conversion under existing national-trust-bank authority; current issuer terms and the August 2026 issuer report state that conversion was completed on December 12, 2025. Paxos describes itself as qualifying under GENIUS and PYUSD as adhering to the standards that will apply when the Act is effective. This is issuer-stated positioning, not a regulator-issued section 5 PPSI approval; issuer-announced-intent and the announced OCC/uninsured-national-trust route are retained. No qualifying official GENIUS approval or issuer application was located in the specifically reviewed sources. The regime remains pre-effective; broad DASP offer/sale restrictions do not become active merely because an issuer is not yet PPSI-approved. EnforcementStatus warning-or-notice records the historical August 7, 2025 NYDFS action against the same converting issuer for AML, transaction-monitoring and Binance-related deficiencies: $26.5 million penalty and at least $22 million remediation spending, with continuing remediation imposed by OCC conversion condition 8. It is not a GENIUS violation finding, PYUSD issuance prohibition, or extension of the historical BUSD mint halt. PayPal advertises loyalty rewards, but the opened OCC proposal does not identify a PayPal/PYUSD-specific enforcement or scrutiny decision; the old coin-specific scrutiny assertion is removed. The transparency hub is issuer disclosure; its linked report contains a separate KPMG examination.

negativeEvidenceReview.summary: As of this review no regulator source inspected identifies a GENIUS section 5 PPSI approval or a qualifying pending PPSI application for PYUSD/Paxos Trust Company, N.A. The OCC conditional conversion authorizes an existing-law trust-bank business, requires future GENIUS compliance and carries historical DFS remediation; it is not a token-specific GENIUS approval. The pending digital-asset charter table is not an exhaustive PPSI register. Paxos issuer statements support intent but do not satisfy the official-approval evidence bar.
